events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The rider cancelled this instant RydeX booking, so NS-0 routes the fee question to NS-4 [F2][F5][NS-0]. The timeline records acceptance at 12:54:00 and rider cancellation at 12:55:40, i.e. 100 seconds after matching [F2], which is inside NS-4's 3-minute (≤ 3:00) free-cancellation window; the trace marks the "more than 3 min after matching" element ✗ [F2][NS-4]. The $6.61 cancellation fee on record therefore has no charging condition and must be returned in full [F5][NS-4].

The driver-side no-show gateway never opened either: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no arrival at the pickup point was recorded [F3][F4][NS-1]. GPS puts the driver's closest approach at 2597 m, never within 200 m of the pickup [F1], so NS-1 (ii) fails on the system record [F1][NS-1]. NS-2 then makes the $6.61 fully refundable to the rider [F5][NS-2].

The driver's written statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" is a post-hoc statement and yields to the GPS and timeline records [F8][F1][F3][F4][NS-1]; it cannot revive the fee and does not affect the outcome.

Amount: the only charged item is the flat $6.61 cancellation fee at 1.0× surge, with no other add-on and no completed-trip component [F5][F6]; $6.61 is the correct refund (Ryde voucher, NS-7) [F5][F6][NS-4][NS-7].

No account flag: NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS places him elsewhere, which F4 rules out [F4][NS-2], and the case against the driver is not "established" for RD-6's repeated-dispute purpose from a single 90-day record [F13][RD-6]. Both advocates withdrew the flag request.

Safety screen: reading the complaint, the driver statement and the (empty) chat, there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the complaint is a fee objection and F8 is a neutral explanation [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. No safety clause applies, so no escalation on that ground [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 1 min 40 s (100 seconds) after acceptance, which is within the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so no cancellation fee is chargeable.
The $6.61 cancellation fee on record must therefore be refunded in full, since the conditions that would make it valid (driver no-show cancellation) are absent.
No driver-no-show can be established: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) and the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null).
GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 2597 m and the driver never came within 200 m, so requirement (ii) of the no-show rule (driver at the pickup point by GPS) fails.
With the no-show elements failing on both the button tap and the GPS location, NS-2 applies and the full $6.61 must be returned to the rider.

The driver's written explanation "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" confirms the driver had not arrived, and is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, so it cannot support a no-show finding.
No chat consent or agreement is in issue: the chat record contains no in-app messages at all.
Refund sizing: the charge is the flat $6.61 cancellation fee with no surge (1.0x) and no other disputed add-on, so the amount computable from the fare facts is exactly SGD 6.61.
The driver's own 90-day record already contains one upheld no-show dispute against them, which supports sending the account for Ryde review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The rider's own 90-day profile shows 3 disputes with 2 upheld no-show disputes (F12), so the judge may read this as a pattern of fee-related filings rather than a one-off error.

The complaint says "within 1 minutes" while the timeline records cancellation at 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2); the discrepancy is trivial relative to the 3-minute threshold, but the other side will point to it to question the rider's account.

The rider did cancel voluntarily rather than waiting for the driver; if the judge treated the driver's "I was on my way" statement (F8) as credible, it would argue some inconvenience — though it cannot revive the fee because F3 and F4 show no arrival and no "I'm Here" tap.

claims.assertion: The rider booked an instant RydeX trip and cancelled 1 min 40 s after matching (12:55:40 vs acceptance at 12:54:00), which is more than 3 minutes short of the free-cancellation window only in the sense that the 3-minute grace period had not yet elapsed — the core NS-0 gateway is instead whether the driver pressed 'I'm Here'; the timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null (F4), so NS-1 was never triggered.

Because the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' (F4) and the platform never recorded arrival at the pickup (F3), the $6.61 cancellation fee cannot be justified under NS-4's 'driver presses I'm Here, waits > 3 minutes then cancels' branch, which requires an unconsummated no-show; here the rider cancelled first, so the fee is unauthorised.

The rider's own complaint that the driver 'was nowhere near' is corroborated by GPS: the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 2597 m and never within 200 m (F1), so the driver cannot assert NS-1's locational requirement and cannot resist the refund on that ground.

The driver's post-hoc statement 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F8) is not a system record and cannot override the GPS and timeline evidence (F1, F3, F4); under the record-priority rule the system records win.

There is no basis for a driver-side counterclaim: the fare record shows only the $6.61 cancellation fee with a 1.0× surge multiplier and no completed-trip component (F5, F6), so no waiting fee or completed-trip earnings are in issue.

Traffic and weather conditions provide no excuse for the driver's distance from the pickup: no incidents were recorded during the trip window (F10) and the only speed-band record is a moderate band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Keppel Road, not a severe-congestion band 1–2 (F9, F11).

The driver's 90-day profile shows only 1 prior dispute (1 upheld, no-show: 1) against 1160 trips (F13); since the profile facts show no pattern of repeated no-show-button abuse, no account-review flag is warranted here, and profile facts cannot decide the case regardless.

weaknesses: The GPS record is fatal to any defended fee: F1 shows the driver's closest approach was 2597 m with never a 200 m entry, and F3 shows no recorded arrival — the other side will use F1/F3 to establish NS-1 (ii) is unsatisfied, forcing refund_full under NS-2.
F4 (driver never pressed 'I'm Here') removes the only route to retaining the fee under NS-1/NS-4; I cannot honestly argue the fee was validly triggered.

My own client's written statement F8 ('I was on my way') conflicts with the GPS in F1 and will be read as an attempt to justify a fee the platform's own records contradict, while the rider's profile (F12: 2 previous no-show disputes upheld) gives the rider a credible history of no-show disputes, though it cannot cure the missing 'I'm Here' tap.

The rider cancelled at 1 min 40 s (F2), i.e. beyond the 3-minute instant-booking free window is not met either way; if the adjudicator reads NS-4 as fee-generating once the rider cancels after matching and before 3 minutes have elapsed, the refund may be reduced — this is an honest risk in my case.

points.response: Agreed the no-show gateway in NS-0/NS-1 was never opened (F3, F4), but that cuts our way: with cancelled_by = rider the only gateway is NS-4, and the cancellation at 12:55:40 was only 1 min 40 s after acceptance (F2), inside the 3-minute free window, so nothing is chargeable.
Conceded: the driver's brief itself finds the $6.61 unauthorised (F3, F4, F5) and that is exactly the relief my client seeks.
Conceded: F1 (closest approach 2597 m, never within 200 m) removes NS-1 (ii) and, read with F2, confirms the fee was collected without any qualifying event.
Conceded: F8 is a post-hoc driver statement and loses to the GPS and timeline records in F1, F3 and F4; it adds nothing that supports the fee.
Conceded: F5 and F6 show one flat $6.61 cancellation fee, 1.0x surge, no completed-trip component, so my claim is limited to that single $6.61 and no waiting fee or fare item arises.
Not in dispute on my side either: F9 is only band 4 (30–39 km/h) and F10 records no incident, so RD-4 gives the driver no excuse — incidental to my case, which rests on NS-4 and NS-2 (F2, F5).

I do not press for a flag_account: my claim C9 is withdrawn, since F13 shows a single prior dispute and profile facts cannot decide the case anyway; I maintain only the full $6.61 refund under NS-2 and NS-4 (F2, F5).
Conceded: F2 records cancellation 1 min 40 s after acceptance at 12:54:00, i.e. within NS-4's 3-minute window, so the $6.61 fee is not chargeable on the rider-cancels branch and I do not contest it.
Conceded: with NS-0's rider-cancel branch routed to NS-4, the fee on record (F5) lacks a valid charging condition and must be refunded in full.
Conceded: F4 (driver_pressed_here_at is null) and F3 (driver_arrived_at is null) mean NS-1 (i) and the recorded arrival element are both absent, so no no-show fee can stand.
Conceded: F1 (closest approach 2597 m, never within 200 m) defeats NS-1 (ii), and I made no contrary argument in my own brief.
Conceded: NS-2 applies and the full $6.61 is to be returned; my brief already requests refund_full $6.61.
I did not rely on F8 and record-priority cuts against my client: the GPS/timeline records in F1, F3 and F4 override the post-hoc statement in F8, so C6 is correct as far as it goes.
Agreed and irrelevant: F7 shows no in-app messages, so RD-5 consent is not in issue and neither side's timing claim depends on chat.
Agreed on sizing: the only charged item computable from the fare facts is the $6.61 cancellation fee on F5, with 1.0× surge per F6 and no other add-on, so $6.61 is the correct refund amount.

This is the one point I contest: flag_account under RD-6 requires a case established against the driver, and here the fee fails on record (F3, F4, F1) precisely because the driver never pressed 'I'm Here' or arrived, while F13 shows 1 dispute in 90 days across 1160 trips; NS-2's account flag attaches only when the driver pressed 'I'm Here' yet GPS shows him elsewhere, which F4 rules out.

Keying off F12, the rider's own profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 2 no-show disputes upheld; I do not use this to resist the refund on this ticket, but it is the reason I ask that any review of account patterns in this case look at both sides' records, not only the driver's.
